title: Efficient classical simulation of two-dimensional long-range systems: Rydberg arrays and beyond
authors: Jia-Lin Chan, Tao Xiang, Yantao Wu
abstract: In variational Monte Carlo (VMC) calculations of $N$-site quantum systems with arbitrary all-to-all two-body interactions, evaluating the local energy generally costs $O(N^3)$. We introduce a new framework that reduces this cost to $O(N)$ for tensor network states, capable of scalable and accurate computation of real-time dynamics and ground states. As a result, we obtain accurate simulations of the adiabatic real-time protocol of a $10\times10$ dipolar XY model realized in a Rydberg simulator [C. Chen et al., Nature 616, 691 (2023)], which was previously beyond the reach of classical simulation. Going beyond quantum experiments, we also directly perform ground state VMC to compare with the adiabatic state preparation. Our work demonstrates tensor network VMC as a powerful classical simulator for long-range quantum platforms such as Rydberg and ion-trap simulators, which are currently in urgent need of scalable classical benchmarking tools. As a separate technical contribution, we resolve the pathology of evolving from product states within of tensor network VMC.
summary: The paper introduces an efficient tensor network Variational Monte Carlo (tVMC) framework that reduces the computational cost for simulating 2D long-range quantum systems from $O(N^3)$ to $O(N)$. This breakthrough allows for accurate, classical simulation of complex adiabatic protocols in dipolar XY models realized in Rydberg arrays. It establishes a powerful new tool for benchmarking next-generation quantum simulators.
main_problem: Developing an efficient classical simulation method for two-dimensional quantum systems with long-range interactions, which is computationally challenging using standard Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) techniques.
main_result: The authors developed a tensor network VMC framework that reduces the local energy evaluation cost from $O(N^3)$ to $O(N)$, enabling accurate simulations of complex protocols previously beyond classical reach.
method: They employ an adapted-basis tensor network tVMC framework, utilizing techniques like projected tVMC (p-tVMC) for initial steps and systematic basis splitting to achieve linear scaling in system size N.
model_or_system: The study focuses on 2D dipolar XY models realized in platforms like Rydberg arrays or ion traps. The Hamiltonian involves long-range, all-to-all two-body interactions ($1/r^3$ coupling).
key_observables: Local energy, sublattice magnetization (Z), nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor correlations ($C_x$), and squared staggered magnetization ($m_x^2$).
important_parameters: System size up to $10 	imes 10$, bond dimension D for TNS, and time evolution parameters ($\Delta t$, $\delta(t)$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the system state can be accurately represented by a Tensor Network State (TNS) ansatz. A technical limitation addressed was the pathology of evolving from product states.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the experimental protocol for the dipolar XY model. Figure 2 benchmarks TNS-tVMC against exact results for smaller systems, showing convergence. Figure 3 shows time evolution and correlations for the $10 	imes 10$ system.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the computational bottleneck ($O(N^3)$) and proposes the novel $O(N)$ tensor network tVMC framework. It details the implementation, including handling initial state projection (p-tVMC), and applies it to simulate adiabatic protocols for dipolar XY models.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial algorithmic breakthrough by scaling classical simulations of long-range quantum systems from cubic to linear complexity, directly enabling benchmarking of cutting-edge hardware like Rydberg arrays.
